floor.source: Jenett et al. 2019 Table 2 — 2,126 t shell on a 4.19e6 m3 lattice sphere. Bare lattice: no skin, joints, valves or plant.

credible.source: Jenett's lattice plus a 50% allowance for the joints, panel attachments and non-spherical geometry the paper excludes and names as later work.

demonstrated.source: Akhmeteli & Gavrilin 2021 — the only vacuum shell design checked against a buckling FEA, at 0.9 x 1.29 kg/m3.

floor.source: Derived by barrier_floor() from the hull's lattice pitch: a Zylon film bulging into one cell at h/a = 0.25, safety factor 4, 50% fibre efficiency.

credible.source: Ten times the derived film floor, for seams, adhesive, handling plies and repair patches. Nobody has made one.

demonstrated.source: Metlen 2013 — Zylon-reinforced Mylar, the only real membrane in the literature, at W/B += 0.37.

floor.source: MicroLink flexible solar sheet, 250 W/m2 at >700 W/kg — flight hardware on Zephyr and PHASA-35.

credible.source: X Development HALE patent US 10,407,153 budgets ~500 g/m2 of cells plus ~150 g/m2 of structure, installed.

demonstrated.source: A conservative installed figure with encapsulation and attachment for a hull that flies through smoke and hail.

floor.source: Lvovich 2020 (NASA GRC) — 'no clear path' beyond 500 Wh/kg at pack level. The best case anyone at NASA will name.

demonstrated.source: Chin et al. 2021, printed p. 2 — a built X-57 pack, from 225 Wh/kg cells at a cell-to-pack factor of 0.66. The electric aircraft did not fly (NASA X-57 Systems Engineering Lessons Learned, printed p. 4).

floor.source: NASA HEMM target, 1.4 MW class. A target, not a delivery.

credible.source: NASA electrified-aircraft metric goal for MW-class machines.

demonstrated.source: Representative of MW-class machines actually run on a bench.

floor.source: A CH-47 blade set plus hub is about 1.4 t on an 18.3 m rotor — 5.3 kg per m2 of disc, and radius-independent under the mass-goes-as-diameter-squared scaling this line assumes. An earlier version used 1.5, which is the blades-only figure and contradicted this string.

credible.source: The same, with a hub and pylon for a body of revolution.

floor.source: NO SOURCE; 34x lighter than the NASA Mars-surface oxygen liquefaction estimate. A stated gift to the budget, not an estimate.

credible.source: NO SOURCE. A three-fold improvement on ground practice.

demonstrated.source: Stirling StirLIN-2, 34 kW in 2,200 kg; comparator: Hauser et al., Table 1, printed p. 3, estimate 136.5 kg at 1,990 W input (68.6 t/MW) for Mars-surface oxygen liquefaction, including cryocooler and radiator; not a flight design.

floor.source: Vacuum-jacketed cryogenic tank at large scale, LN2 (denser and warmer than LH2, so lighter per tonne stored).

credible.source: The same with structure to react flight loads.

floor.source: Coated fabric for water bladders and the anchor bag.

credible.source: The same, with wear plies at the fill and dump interfaces.

floor.source: UHMWPE at 2.0 N/tex — the optimistic end of realised rope tenacity.

credible.source: Commercial 12-strand UHMWPE data sheets realise 1.4-1.6 N/tex, well under the 3.5-4.0 N/tex of the bare fibre.

demonstrated.source: The pessimistic end of the same data sheets.

floor.source: Reinforced layflat discharge hose, mass per metre per metre of bore, at the 30 bar this head needs.

credible.source: The same in a wire-reinforced construction that survives repeated deployment.

floor.source: Sentinel 1000 actuals: electrics, instruments and miscellaneous are 9.9% of empty weight on a flown airship.

demonstrated.source: With an ANSI/AIAA S-120 mass growth allowance on top.
